hero.headline: Supreme Court nears end of term with major cases still undecided
hero.body:
The Supreme Court is entering its final weeks, a period when justices typically race to complete their most significant rulings before the summer recess. The court has issued several consequential decisions as the term winds down, with more opinions expected in the coming days.

One of the most significant recent rulings came in a case involving Alabama's congressional map. In a 6-3 decision, the court's conservative majority allowed Alabama to use a redrawn map that eliminates one of the state's two majority-Black districts in upcoming midterm elections. The unsigned opinion marked another major blow to voting rights protections and represented a significant victory for Republicans.

The decision came after the court's landmark April ruling in Louisiana v Callais, which struck down a critical provision of the Voting Rights Act. In that case, the court made it nearly impossible to win voting rights claims by requiring plaintiffs to prove intentional discrimination. The Alabama ruling applied this new standard, reversing a lower court's May 26 decision that had blocked the state's map as intentionally discriminatory.

The court's conservative justices argued that the three-judge panel had failed to properly reconsider the case under the Callais decision and other recent rulings weakening the Voting Rights Act. They noted that the lower court had failed to give the legislature a presumption of good faith and had not properly evaluate whether an alternative map offered by plaintiffs could perform as well as the state's map on neutral redistricting criteria.

The three liberal justices issued a sharply worded dissent. Justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson, accused the majority of causing chaos and abandoning the rule of law. She contrasted two paths forward: one with an orderly election under a map protecting Black voters' rights, and another with a chaotic election under a map intentionally discriminating against Black voters. "The majority chooses the second path and disregards both democratic values and the rule of law," Sotomayor wrote.

The ruling concluded a lengthy legal battle over Alabama's congressional map. After the 2020 census, Alabama created a plan with only one majority-Black district. Black voters challenged this, and courts previously ordered the state to create two majority-Black districts. When Alabama Republicans redrew the map in 2023, they again created only one majority-Black district. The court blocked that map and appointed a special master to draw a compliant plan with two majority-Black districts, which was used in the 2024 election.

Following the Callais decision, Alabama sought to reinstate its 2023 map, leading to the latest court battle. The Supreme Court's decision allows the state to proceed with its plan despite the lower court's finding of discriminatory intent.

cards.headline: U.S.-Iran war reaches 100 days with no resolution
cards.teaser: The conflict between the United States and Iran has continued for over three months despite Trump's campaign pledges to avoid prolonged foreign wars.
cards.body:
The war between the United States and Iran reached its 100-day mark over the weekend with no clear path to resolution. President Trump had campaigned on promises to keep the country out of extended foreign conflicts.

Trump responded to questions about the war's duration by denying he had ever promised not to start new wars. He also disputed characterizations of the conflict with Iran as an endless war. The fighting has now extended well beyond initial expectations, with no timeline for conclusion.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon as Hezbollah Campaign Complicates US-Iran Peace Talks
cards.body:
Israel carried out fresh airstrikes on southern Lebanon on Tuesday while ordering residents of 16 villages to evacuate northward, as fighting persisted despite a ceasefire agreement reached in April. The military operations targeted areas where Hezbollah maintains a significant presence.

Hezbollah responded with drone attacks on Israeli soldiers in the region, claiming to have injured several troops. The Lebanese militia has deployed small, fiber-optic-guided drones that have proven difficult for Israeli air defenses to intercept. These wired aircraft produce limited radio signals that evade radar detection and have a range of up to 9 miles. Since the ceasefire began on April 17, Hezbollah has used the drones to attack Israeli soldiers almost daily in southern Lebanon.

The fighting has resulted in substantial casualties. Israeli airstrikes killed 18 people and wounded 88 more in Lebanon over the weekend alone. Since the conflict between Hezbollah and Israel began on March 2, at least 2,534 people have been killed and 7,863 wounded in Lebanon, according to the Lebanese health ministry. Hezbollah rocket fire has killed two Israeli civilians during the same period.

The continued military operations have become a significant complication for broader diplomatic efforts. Negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stating that any permanent ceasefire must include a nuclear agreement with Iran. The tensions have undermined attempts to use the Lebanon ceasefire as a stepping stone to wider regional peace.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended the military campaign, saying Hezbollah's remaining weapons continue to threaten northern Israel. "They have about 10% of the missiles they had at the start of the war. But these still trouble the residents of the north," Netanyahu said. He pledged further strikes against what he characterized as Hezbollah infrastructure. Israeli media reported that Netanyahu told President Trump that Israel needed to respond to maintain restraint from the armed group. The US subsequently asked Israel to ensure any response remained "calculated and limited."

The ceasefire agreement included a clause allowing Israel to conduct strikes in self-defense, a provision Israel has used extensively. The text covers a "yellow line" security zone in southern Lebanon where Israeli troops operate across at least 55 villages. Israel has continued demolishing homes in this area.

Lebanon's government faces significant challenges controlling the situation. The Lebanese government negotiated the ceasefire with Israel in Washington but has little ability to influence Hezbollah's actions. Hezbollah has rejected the direct negotiations, with group leader Naim Qassem calling them a "grave sin" on Monday. The group has refused to disarm, a key Israeli demand, stating the negotiations do not concern them.

cards.headline: US and Iran Struggle to Frame Potential Deal as Victory
cards.teaser: Both Washington and Tehran face domestic pressure to present any agreement as a win, complicating ongoing peace negotiations.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran face a fundamental challenge in their peace negotiations: both nations need to present any agreement to their domestic audiences as a victory rather than a compromise.

This dynamic complicates already difficult talks between the two countries. Washington and Tehran each have leaders whose negotiating approach has frustrated mediators attempting to bridge decades of hostility and mistrust. Neither side can afford to appear weak by accepting significant concessions without securing visible gains of their own, making it harder to find common ground.

cards.headline: Congress faces deadline to renew warrantless surveillance powers
cards.teaser: A deadline to reauthorize Section 702 surveillance powers collides with controversy over a White House intelligence appointment.
cards.body:
The deadline to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is approaching as Democrats increasingly oppose reauthorization due to the White House appointment of Bill Pulte to lead the intelligence community. The warrantless spy powers allow intelligence agencies to monitor foreign targets.

A growing number of Democrats have said they will not vote to renew Section 702 while Pulte's appointment remains in place. The collision between the reauthorization deadline and the pressure campaign over Pulte's nomination creates uncertainty about whether Congress will extend the surveillance authority before it expires.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Israel and Iran Agree to Halt Strikes
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined after Israel and Iran reached an agreement to stop military strikes against each other, reducing fears of wider regional conflict.
cards.body:
Oil prices eased following an agreement between Israel and Iran to halt strikes against each other, calming market concerns about supply disruptions from a broader Middle East conflict. The brief spike in crude prices reversed as geopolitical tensions appeared to de-escalate.

The agreement removes immediate pressure on oil markets that had been pricing in the risk of expanded military action affecting Persian Gulf shipping lanes and energy infrastructure. Energy traders had pushed prices higher on fears that sustained conflict could disrupt the flow of crude from one of the world's most important producing regions.

cards.headline: Trump nominates Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.body:
President Trump formally nominated Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general on Monday, positioning his former personal lawyer to become the nation's top law enforcement officer. The nomination will require Senate confirmation to become permanent.

Blanche has been serving in an acting capacity since April, when Trump fired Pam Bondi from the role. Bondi faced criticism for her handling of the Epstein files, an issue that has followed the president for years. Trump previously described Blanche as "a very talented guy" while discussing the nomination on a podcast.

Blanche previously represented Trump in several high-profile legal cases. He was Trump's attorney in the hush-money case involving adult film actor Stormy Daniels, which resulted in Trump's conviction on 34 felony counts for fraudulently falsifying business records. Blanche also represented Trump in the federal classified documents case and election obstruction cases, both of which were dismissed following Trump's electoral victory.

As acting attorney general, Blanche has pursued controversial actions under the banner of combating what the administration calls "weaponization" of the Justice Department. Federal prosecutors have filed criminal charges against James Comey, the former FBI director, and escalated investigations into former CIA director John Brennan. The department also removed press releases about prosecutions related to the January 6 Capitol attack.

Republican Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Chuck Grassley called Blanche "well-qualified," stating he has "worked well with acting attorney general Blanche for more than a year and appreciate his commitment to transparency and support for law enforcement."

Democratic opposition is expected to be significant. Senator Adam Schiff of California argued that "at every turn, Todd Blanche has been unable to put aside his role as Donald Trump's criminal defense lawyer and represent the American people instead." Schiff highlighted several controversial decisions, including support for the Comey indictment based on an Instagram photo and approval of a 1.8 billion dollar fund to compensate Trump supporters who claimed they faced political persecution.

Blanche also signed a Justice Department memo granting Trump, his sons, and the Trump Organization immunity from IRS audits and tax prosecutions. Representative Rosa DeLauro, a Connecticut Democrat, criticized this action, saying that "when you are issuing memos granting the president, his children, and their companies immunity from audits or prosecution for tax offenses, your previous role becomes relevant information."

The controversial compensation fund faced bipartisan criticism. Republican Brian Fitzpatrick from Pennsylvania drafted legislation with bipartisan support to block its creation. Under mounting pressure, Blanche announced on Tuesday that the fund had been terminated.

Republicans hold the Senate majority, which could facilitate confirmation, though some lawmakers have indicated they plan to review Blanche's record closely. The Senate Judiciary Committee typically schedules hearings within weeks of a formal nomination.

cards.headline: Drones From Russia-Ukraine War Stray Into Neighboring Countries
cards.teaser: Unmanned aircraft launched by both sides in the conflict are flying off course and threatening nations not involved in the war.
cards.body:
Both Russian and Ukrainian forces are deploying drones that frequently veer off course and cross into neighboring countries not involved in the conflict. These unintended incursions have raised alarm among Ukraine's border nations about the growing risks of drone warfare.

The incidents underscore the challenges of maintaining control over unmanned aircraft in active combat zones. Navigation errors and technical failures can send drones across international borders, forcing neighboring countries to grapple with how to defend their airspace and protect their populations from these unintended threats.

cards.headline: Kenyan Police Use Tear Gas on Protesters Opposing US Ebola Center
cards.teaser: Demonstrators voiced concerns about infection risks and lack of government transparency regarding a planned treatment facility.
cards.body:
Kenyan police used tear gas to disperse protesters opposing a US-funded Ebola quarantine center in their region. The demonstrators raised concerns about the risk of cross-border disease transmission and questioned the government's transparency regarding the facility's plans and operations.

Local residents expressed worry about hosting an infectious disease treatment center in proximity to their communities. The protesters indicated they had not been adequately informed about the project before authorities moved forward with plans.

cards.headline: Lebanese City of Nabatieh Faces Uncertain Future Amid Continuing War
cards.teaser: The once-thriving city now reflects Lebanon's deepest fears as conflict grinds on without resolution.
cards.body:
The city of Nabatieh, which once served as a symbol of Lebanon's changing fortunes, now embodies the country's worst fears as war continues without end. The city's current state reflects the broader devastation that prolonged conflict has brought to Lebanon.

Nabatieh had been a thriving urban center before the escalation of regional conflicts. Its transformation illustrates the human and economic toll that unending warfare has imposed on Lebanese communities caught in the crossfire of larger geopolitical struggles.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup Ticket Allocation Revoked Days Before Tournament
cards.teaser: The Iranian football federation said its tickets for the group stage were taken back just before the competition begins.
cards.body:
Iran's football federation announced that its ticket allocation for the World Cup group stage has been revoked just days before the tournament begins. The decision leaves Iranian fans unable to attend their national team's matches during the opening round of competition.

The timing of the revocation provides minimal opportunity for the federation or supporters to arrange alternative plans. This sudden withdrawal of access affects what would have been a significant presence of Iranian supporters at the tournament.

cards.headline: Somali World Cup Referee Denied Entry to United States
cards.teaser: Omar Artan was set to become the first Somali to officiate at the World Cup finals before being barred from entering the US.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a Somali referee, has been removed from the World Cup officials list after US authorities denied him entry to the country. Artan would have made history as the first Somali national to referee at a World Cup finals tournament.

The denial of entry meant Artan missed the opportunity to participate in one of football's most prestigious events.

cards.headline: Cancer survival rates rise, but mental health challenges linger for survivors
cards.teaser: Advances in treatment and screening have led to more Americans surviving cancer, though many face ongoing psychological impacts.
cards.body:
More Americans are surviving cancer due to advancements in treatment and screening methods. This progress represents a significant achievement in oncology and public health.

However, many cancer survivors face persistent mental health challenges long after their treatment concludes. Anxiety and depression are common psychological effects that can linger for years, impacting survivors' quality of life despite improvements in their physical health.

cards.headline: Weight loss drugs show promise in cancer prevention and treatment
cards.teaser: Recent studies suggest GLP-1 medications may prevent cancer and slow its progression through multiple pathways.
cards.body:
GLP-1 drugs, used for weight loss and diabetes treatment, appear to both prevent cancer and slow its progression according to recent research. While weight loss itself reduces cancer risk, scientists believe these medications may work through additional mechanisms.

Researchers are investigating how GLP-1s might act on brain and metabolic pathways beyond their weight loss effects. The drugs could offer new approaches to cancer prevention and treatment if the protective mechanisms are confirmed through further study.

cards.headline: Updated California vote counts reveal county-by-county results in governor primary
cards.teaser: New tallies show how each California county voted in the state's gubernatorial primary election.
cards.body:
Updated vote counts from California's gubernatorial primary election have been released, showing voting patterns across all counties in the state. The tallies provide a detailed breakdown of how different regions supported candidates in the race.

California's ballot counting process has drawn attention for its extended timeline compared to other states. The state's mail-in ballot system and verification procedures mean final results can take days or weeks to compile after election day.

---

Note: The additional source material provided does not contain relevant information about the California governor primary vote counts. The first source discusses fraud allegations, and the second is an obituary. Therefore, I'm returning the original card text unchanged.

cards.headline: Nithya Raman advances to runoff against Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass
cards.teaser: Progressive City Council member Nithya Raman secured second place in the Los Angeles mayoral race and will face the incumbent in November.
cards.body:
Nithya Raman, a progressive Los Angeles city council member, has advanced to the November runoff for LA mayor after edging out former reality TV star Spencer Pratt for second place. Pratt had initially held a lead following the primary election, but as additional ballots were processed, Raman pulled ahead.

Raman will now face incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in a general election runoff that will determine Los Angeles's next leader. The November contest pits two candidates with different governing approaches against each other for control of the nation's second-largest city.

cards.headline: Primary elections underway in Maine, Nevada and South Carolina
cards.teaser: Voters in three states are casting ballots in primary contests including a Senate race and a gubernatorial election.
cards.body:
Primary elections are underway in Maine, Nevada and South Carolina. Republican incumbents are facing significant challenges in both Maine and Nevada as voters head to the polls.

In South Carolina, a large group of Republican candidates are competing in the gubernatorial primary. The candidates have positioned themselves as devoted to the MAGA movement as they seek their party's nomination for governor.

cards.headline: Some Maine Democrats express concerns about Senate candidate Graham Platner
cards.teaser: Maine Democrats are deciding whether to support their party's Senate candidate amid questions about past allegations.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, the Democratic Senate candidate in Maine, faces wavering support from some party members. The candidate has been dogged by allegations related to past actions that have generated controversy.

Representative Ro Khanna condemned Platner's past actions but noted they did not come as a surprise to Maine voters. Despite the concerns, some supporters continue to back Platner's campaign, though with expressed reservations about the allegations.

hero.headline: OpenAI Files for Public Stock Offering in Major AI Market Move
hero.body:
OpenAI has confidentially submitted paperwork to go public on the US stock market, the company announced Monday through a blog post. The artificial intelligence company behind ChatGPT is expected to become one of the most highly valued listings in market history, with a valuation exceeding $850 billion.

"We recently submitted a confidential S-1. We expect it to leak so we're just announcing it," OpenAI stated in the announcement. The company added that it has not yet decided on timing for the public offering, noting that "there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company."

The confidential filing, known as a Form S-1, allows OpenAI to submit its investor prospectus to the Securities and Exchange Commission for regulatory review while keeping financial details private until closer to the actual listing date. This approach gives regulators time to discuss and review the company's financial disclosures before the public sees them.

OpenAI's move comes just over a week after rival Anthropic, which produces the Claude chatbot, announced its own plans to go public. The back-to-back filings mark an acceleration in the competition between leading AI companies to access public markets as they scale operations and vie for dominance in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence industry.

The timing reflects OpenAI's dramatic trajectory since its founding in 2015 as a non-profit research lab under CEO Sam Altman. After releasing ChatGPT publicly in 2022 and converting to a for-profit structure, the company rapidly accumulated hundreds of millions of users and fundamentally changed how people work across entertainment, healthcare, education, and employment sectors.

OpenAI achieved its current valuation of around $852 billion after closing a $122 billion funding round in March, according to the Wall Street Journal. The company reached this valuation despite reported difficulties turning a profit and missing key revenue and user acquisition targets.

The IPO announcement arrives as OpenAI has continued securing major partnerships with companies including Microsoft, Google, and Nvidia, as well as with the Trump administration. The company recently acquired iPhone designer Jony Ive's startup for billions in stock, though efforts to expand beyond ChatGPT have produced mixed results, including the shutdown of its Sora video generation app in April 2026.

OpenAI also recently prevailed in a lawsuit brought by Elon Musk, who sought to force the company to revert to non-profit status. A jury panel ruled that the case fell outside the statute of limitations.

Another major AI competitor, SpaceX and Elon Musk's xAI, is also expected to go public at a valuation around $1.75 trillion, promising to make this a significant year for AI company debuts on Wall Street.

cards.headline: Pentagon Adds BYD and Alibaba to Chinese Military Companies List
cards.teaser: The Defense Department designated major Chinese tech firms including electric carmaker BYD and e-commerce giant Alibaba as companies supporting China's military.
cards.body:
The Pentagon designated several major Chinese technology firms as supporting China's military, including electric vehicle manufacturer BYD, e-commerce giant Alibaba, search engine Baidu, and robotics company Unitree. The designation prevents these companies from securing U.S. defense contracts.

The updated list was initially released by the Trump administration four months prior but was quickly removed without explanation. The Pentagon's military companies list warns U.S. firms of potential risks and national security concerns associated with doing business with the flagged Chinese entities.

cards.headline: China's Exports Jump on Semiconductor and AI Demand
cards.teaser: Chinese export growth exceeded forecasts in May, driven by surging demand for semiconductors and AI-related technology products.
cards.body:
I can see the Bloomberg source headline confirms the core story about China's export surge driven by AI and tech demand, with the 35% growth to the U.S. mentioned. However, the actual article text from Bloomberg wasn't provided—only the headline.

The BBC sources are about different stories (Meta's AI leadership and child safety on phones), so they don't apply here.

Since I can only verify the headline details and not the full article content, I should return your original card text unchanged:

China reported stronger than expected export growth for May, propelled by booming demand for semiconductors, rare earth materials, and technology products tied to artificial intelligence development. Shipments to the United States climbed 35 percent, marking the highest growth rate to the U.S. in five years.

The export surge reflects China's strengthening position in semiconductor manufacturing and rare earth supply chains, both critical to AI technology production. The trade data shows China benefiting from the global AI boom even as geopolitical tensions continue between Beijing and Washington over technology competition and national security concerns.

cards.headline: States Prepare Antitrust Lawsuit Against Paramount-Warner Bros Merger
cards.teaser: California and New York are readying a lawsuit to block Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, citing competition concerns.
cards.body:
Multiple U.S. states led by California and New York are preparing to file an antitrust lawsuit challenging Paramount's proposed $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, according to sources familiar with the matter. The deal is also under investigation by regulators in the United Kingdom.

Paramount has pushed back against opposition to the merger, with company representatives criticizing what they called fear-mongering and partisan politics surrounding the transaction. The Teamsters union has warned about potential job losses and market concentration if the deal proceeds, while Paramount has also directed criticism at Netflix's market position in its defense of the acquisition.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Israel and Iran Agree to Halt Strikes
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined after Israel and Iran reached an agreement to stop military strikes against each other, reducing fears of wider regional conflict.
cards.body:
Oil prices eased following an agreement between Israel and Iran to halt strikes against each other, calming market concerns about supply disruptions from a broader Middle East conflict. The brief spike in crude prices reversed as geopolitical tensions appeared to de-escalate.

The agreement removes immediate pressure on oil markets that had been pricing in the risk of expanded military action affecting Persian Gulf shipping lanes and energy infrastructure. Energy traders had pushed prices higher on fears that sustained conflict could disrupt the flow of crude from one of the world's most important producing regions.

cards.headline: Chip Stocks Recover After Recent Declines
cards.teaser: Semiconductor stocks rebounded as investors bought shares following recent drops, lifting Asian and U.S. chip-related equities.
cards.body:
Chip stocks recovered in Asian and U.S. markets after investors purchased shares at lower prices following recent declines in the sector. Technology stocks broadly gained as concerns about valuations in AI-related companies eased temporarily.

The rebound in semiconductor shares helped lift broader market indexes, with futures pointing to gains in major U.S. stock benchmarks. The rally follows a period of volatility in technology stocks as investors reassess valuations in companies tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure and development.

cards.headline: Treasury Markets Signal Higher Rate Expectations for Fed Chair Warsh
cards.teaser: Bond market pricing suggests Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh may face pressure to keep interest rates elevated despite administration preferences.
cards.body:
Treasury market movements indicate investor expectations that Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh will need to maintain higher interest rates than the administration might prefer, according to market analysts. Bond yields have been signaling that rate cuts may need to wait longer than previously anticipated.

Warsh faces a complicated environment as he approaches his first policy meeting as Fed chair, with market participants watching closely for signals about the central bank's rate path. The bond market is pricing in expectations that economic conditions may require keeping rates higher to manage inflation, potentially putting Warsh at odds with political pressure for lower borrowing costs.

hero.headline: Apple releases Siri AI upgrade with new partnership for advanced model
hero.body:
Apple unveiled a significantly redesigned Siri at its annual developer conference, marking a major shift in the company's approach to artificial intelligence. The upgraded voice assistant, now called Siri AI, will be integrated with Apple's broader artificial intelligence tool known as Apple Intelligence and is scheduled for widespread release in the fall.

The new Siri functions more like modern AI chatbots such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini rather than a traditional web-based question-and-answer tool. Mike Rockwell, Apple's vice president of Siri engineering, demonstrated the assistant's expanded capabilities during the conference, showing how it can handle complex tasks across multiple apps within a single interface. In one demonstration, Rockwell asked Siri to identify a beach location from a photo, find a friend's address, and then provide directions to the beach with a stop at the friend's house.

The revamped assistant represents a notable partnership strategy for Apple. The company is powering Siri AI through Google's Gemini model as part of a billion-dollar partnership between the two tech giants. This collaborative approach marks a shift for Apple, which traditionally develops core technologies internally.

Siri AI will function as a dedicated app available on iPhones, iPads, and laptops. The assistant can handle various tasks including proofreading, shopping, adding calendar events, and using the camera to extract information like nutrition data from food. Currently, the tool will only be available in English.

Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice president of software engineering, acknowledged that some competitors have moved faster in the AI race. "Some appear to be racing forward, seemingly pursuing AI for the sake of AI, without clear regard for the people that it's ultimately meant to serve," he said. Apple has previously postponed Siri updates and faced legal challenges over past advertising claims about the assistant's capabilities, settling a class-action lawsuit for $250 million in May.

The announcements came during what will be Tim Cook's final keynote as CEO before stepping down in the fall after 15 years leading the company. Beyond Siri, Apple introduced new child safety features for its devices, including parental controls that limit what content children can access and who they can communicate with. Parents can use a setup assistant to customize restrictions and gradually expand access as children age.

Apple also integrated AI capabilities into Safari, messaging, the Home app, and photography tools. These features were developed in collaboration with Google, further demonstrating the company's shift toward strategic partnerships in its AI development strategy rather than pursuing all capabilities independently.

cards.headline: iOS 27 code references foldable iPhone features
cards.teaser: Apple's latest iOS beta includes code suggesting the company is developing a foldable iPhone.
cards.body:
Apple's iOS 27 software includes multiple references to a foldable iPhone, according to code found in the beta release. The software contains new framework strings and features related to app resizability, suggesting Apple is preparing its operating system for devices with folding screens.

At WWDC 2026, Apple focused its announcements on improvements to Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The foldable iPhone references represent the first concrete evidence in Apple's software that the company is actively testing such hardware internally, following competitors like Samsung who have sold foldable devices for years.

cards.headline: Instagram adds feature to reorder posts on profile grid
cards.teaser: Meta's Instagram now allows users to rearrange the order of posts displayed on their profile pages.
cards.body:
Instagram released a feature allowing users to reorganize posts on their profile grids. The update lets people change the order in which their photos and videos appear on their public profiles, giving users more control over how their content is presented.

The feature rolled out widely on June 8th via the Android and iPhone mobile apps after being tested with select users. Previously, Instagram posts appeared in reverse chronological order on profile pages, with the most recent content at the top. Users can now manually arrange posts regardless of when they were originally published.

cards.headline: FCC waives deadline for Amazon satellite broadband project
cards.teaser: The Federal Communications Commission lifted a deadline requirement for Amazon's Leo satellite constellation.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission granted Amazon a waiver that removes a deadline for its Leo satellite broadband constellation. According to the FCC, the decision serves the public interest by promoting competition through a second large satellite broadband network.

Amazon's Leo project will deliver internet service via satellites in low Earth orbit. The waiver allows Amazon to continue development without facing regulatory penalties for missing previous deployment timelines.

cards.headline: Jupiter and Venus appear close together in night sky
cards.teaser: The two planets will appear nearly touching in a conjunction visible without telescopes.
cards.body:
Jupiter and Venus will appear extremely close together in the night sky in what astronomers call a conjunction. The two planets will seem to nearly touch when viewed from Earth, creating one of the most visible astronomical events of 2026. No telescope is needed to observe the phenomenon.

The conjunction occurs when planets appear close together in the sky from Earth's perspective, though they remain millions of miles apart in space. Venus and Jupiter are among the brightest objects visible in the night sky, making their close approach particularly striking for observers.

cards.headline: Evotrex raises $30 million for hybrid RV system
cards.teaser: The startup is building recreational vehicles with a power system designed to work beyond traditional campsites.
cards.body:
Evotrex has raised $30 million to develop hybrid RVs that operate independently from charging stations. The startup's power system allows vehicles to function in remote areas beyond traditional campsites, reducing reliance on established infrastructure.

The company enters a competitive RV market alongside other startups modernizing the industry. Evotrex's hybrid approach differentiates it by enabling self-sufficient power generation and storage rather than dependence on external charging networks or conventional fuel alone.

cards.headline: Zepto files for IPO showing revenue growth and widening losses
cards.teaser: The company's advertising revenue grew 151 percent while operating revenue increased 104 percent.
cards.body:
Zepto has filed for an initial public offering, revealing significant growth across its business. The company's advertising revenue grew 151 percent, substantially outpacing its 104 percent increase in operating revenue. However, Zepto continues to operate at a loss despite this expansion.

The IPO filing did not include a proposed share price or valuation range, leaving a key question unanswered about the company's worth in the eyes of its leadership.

hero.headline: Spurs defeat Knicks 115-111 in Game 3, trail Finals 2-1
hero.body:
Victor Wembanyama delivered a breakout performance to lead the San Antonio Spurs past the New York Knicks 115-111 in Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden, snapping New York's 13-game postseason winning streak and cutting the series deficit to 2-1.

Wembanyama finished with 32 points, eight rebounds, six assists and three blocks, his best effort of the series so far. Stephon Castle contributed 23 points and hit two crucial free throws with 6.8 seconds remaining in the third quarter. For the Knicks, Jalen Brunson scored 32 points and OG Anunoby added 28, but the rest of the roster struggled in the fourth quarter, going just 3 for 20 from the field.

The game unfolded against an extraordinary backdrop at Madison Square Garden, with the first NBA Finals game in New York since 1999 drawing high-profile attendees including the sitting U.S. president, Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and numerous celebrities. The atmosphere created an intense environment that tested both teams' focus.

After a difficult Game 2 in which he missed a potential game-winner, Wembanyama entered Game 3 with renewed energy. "Really tried to relax," he said of his approach after the previous loss. "The playoffs, it's like a whirlwind. It's hard to put your head out of the water." He started strong, scoring nine points in his opening nine minutes.

The Spurs built an 11-point first-quarter lead before the Knicks responded aggressively, outscoring San Antonio 42-24 in the second quarter to take a 64-57 halftime advantage. The third quarter remained competitive, with neither team establishing a significant cushion.

The fourth quarter proved decisive. While Brunson contributed 12 points in the final period to keep New York close, his teammates couldn't provide enough support. The Knicks' frustration grew over foul call discrepancies, with chants of "refs, you suck!" breaking out multiple times. New York took just eight free throws in the second half compared to 24 for San Antonio.

Outside of Wembanyama and Castle, the Spurs benefited from the Knicks' 13 turnovers, which resulted in 21 points. Karl-Anthony Towns finished with just 11 points and eight rebounds after consecutive double-doubles in San Antonio, while the rest of the Knicks' supporting cast struggled.

Brunson acknowledged the setback but remained focused on improvement. "We've done our best to try to learn from wins over the past couple weeks. But now we have to learn from a loss," he said.

The series continues with Game 4 on Wednesday in New York. The Knicks need two more wins to clinch the championship, while the Spurs must win consecutive games to force the series back to San Antonio.

cards.headline: Iran's World Cup ticket allocation revoked days before tournament
cards.teaser: Iran's football federation says its allocation of tickets for the World Cup group stage has been withdrawn just days before the tournament begins.
cards.body:
Iran's football federation says its ticket allocation for the World Cup group stage has been revoked just days before the tournament begins. The withdrawal means Iranian fans will not receive their allocated tickets for matches during the group stage.

The timing of the revocation comes as a significant development ahead of the competition's start. Iran is set to participate in the tournament despite the ticket allocation being pulled.

cards.headline: Somali referee Omar Artan barred from entering US, dropped from World Cup
cards.teaser: Omar Artan, who was set to become the first Somali to referee at a World Cup finals, has been dropped from the officials list after being denied entry to the United States.
cards.body:
Omar Artan, a Somali referee who was poised to become the first official from Somalia to work at a World Cup finals, has been removed from the tournament's officials list. His removal came after he was denied entry to the United States, where the World Cup is being held.

Since the tournament requires officials to be physically present in the host country, Artan's inability to enter the US made his participation impossible. He has consequently been dropped from the list of referees for the competition.

cards.headline: Michael Olise scores hat-trick for France against Northern Ireland
cards.teaser: Michael Olise scored his first international hat-trick as France defeated Northern Ireland, with former striker Louis Saha saying the performance puts him in Ballon d'Or contention.
cards.body:
Bayern Munich's Michael Olise scored three goals as France defeated Northern Ireland 3-1 in a World Cup warm-up match in Lille. It was Olise's first international hat-trick.

Former France striker Louis Saha has suggested the performance marks a significant moment in Olise's career, believing it could elevate him into Ballon d'Or contention as he continues to establish himself at the highest level of international football.

cards.headline: Defending champion Tatjana Maria goes through Queen's qualifying to reach main draw
cards.teaser: Tatjana Maria says Queen's should show more respect to defending champions after she was required to go through qualifying to reach the main draw.
cards.body:
Tatjana Maria earned her place in the Queen's main draw after competing through the qualifying rounds, despite being the tournament's defending champion. The German player expressed frustration with the decision, arguing that the tournament should afford greater respect to its title holders.

Maria's comments highlighted the unusual situation where last year's winner was required to go through the same qualifying process as other players seeking entry to the main draw.

cards.headline: RFU council member resigns after discriminatory post about Maggie Alphonsi
cards.teaser: Rugby Football Union council member Matthew Smith has resigned after posting discriminatory criticism of television pundit Maggie Alphonsi.
cards.body:
Matthew Smith has resigned from his position on the Rugby Football Union council following the publication of discriminatory comments he posted about television pundit Maggie Alphonsi. Alphonsi works as a rugby broadcaster covering the sport.

Smith's resignation came after his posts targeting Alphonsi became public, prompting his departure from the RFU council.

cards.headline: Multiple drivers penalized for pit-lane speeding at Monaco Grand Prix
cards.teaser: A high number of drivers received penalties for pit-lane speeding during the Monaco Grand Prix, prompting questions about the frequency of violations.
cards.body:
The Monaco Grand Prix saw an unusually high number of drivers penalized for exceeding the speed limit in the pit lane. BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson addressed questions about why so many drivers were caught for the infraction.

The penalties affected multiple competitors during the race weekend. The pit-lane speed limit is strictly enforced at all Formula 1 events, but Monaco saw a particularly high rate of violations.

hero.headline: Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater end relationship after three years
hero.body:
Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater have separated after three years together, ending a relationship that began on the set of the first Wicked film. The pair met while working on the movie adaptation of the popular Broadway musical, which led to Grande receiving an Oscar nomination for her performance.

The relationship attracted significant public attention when it began in 2023, as both Grande and Slater were ending previous relationships at the time. Grande was married to real estate agent Dalton Gomez, while Slater was married to his high school sweetheart Lilly Jay, with whom he shares a son. The timing of their romance sparked widespread media coverage and public discussion.

Grande's role in Wicked marked a significant moment in her career transition from pop music to film acting. She portrayed Glinda the Good Witch in the adaptation directed by Jon M. Chu. The first Wicked film became one of the highest-grossing musical films, earning $765 million in worldwide box office receipts and winning two Academy Awards. Her performance earned critical acclaim and led to her first Oscar nomination, cementing her status as a multifaceted entertainer capable of success across different mediums.

Slater, a Broadway veteran who originated the role of SpongeBob SquarePants in the musical adaptation, played Boq in the Wicked film. He had built a respected career in theater before transitioning to film work. The couple had largely kept their relationship private in recent months, making few public appearances together.

The end of their relationship comes as the Wicked sequel has performed markedly differently from its predecessor. Wicked: For Good took $541 million at the worldwide box office and received no Oscar nominations, a significant decrease from the first film's performance and accolades.

Recent weeks have seen notable developments surrounding the Wicked cast. During the Singapore premiere of Wicked: For Good, co-star Cynthia Erivo stepped in when a red-carpet invader rushed towards Grande. Erivo described the moment as frightening for both herself and Grande, noting that the intruder would not let go of Grande. The individual was sentenced to nine days in jail.

Erivo later discussed how social media reactions to the incident revealed problematic perceptions of Black women. She explained that comments suggesting she was Grande's bodyguard reflected assumptions about her appearance and role. Erivo said she felt her instinctive protective action had been mischaracterized, noting that the experience discouraged her from campaigning for Oscar recognition for the sequel.

Neither Grande nor Slater has publicly commented on their separation. Grande continues to balance her music career with acting projects, while Slater remains active in both film and theater work.

cards.headline: South Korean director Lee Chang-dong to receive lifetime achievement award at Malaysia film festival
cards.teaser: The filmmaker will be honored at the 9th Malaysia International Film Festival in July.
cards.body:
Lee Chang-dong will receive the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 9th Malaysia International Film Festival, organizers announced while unveiling the full program lineup in Kuala Lumpur. The South Korean filmmaker joins a roster of celebrated directors who have been recognized by the festival for their contributions to cinema.

MIFFest will run from July 18 through 25 and will present 65 films from 35 countries and regions in 27 languages. The festival program includes two world premieres and one international premiere, showcasing a diverse selection of global cinema in Malaysia's capital.

cards.headline: Chelsea players Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro appear in Madonna promotional video
cards.teaser: The footballers made a surprise cameo in a film promoting the pop star's new album.
cards.body:
Chelsea forwards Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro have made a surprise appearance in a promotional film for Madonna's new album. The unexpected crossover brings together football and music, featuring the two Premier League players in the video alongside the iconic performer.

The collaboration marks an unusual partnership between the worlds of sport and pop music, with the players featuring in the promotional content for Madonna's latest musical release.

cards.headline: Chaka Khan and Simple Minds to headline Radio 2 festival in Scotland
cards.teaser: The three-day music event will take place in Stirling in September.
cards.body: Chaka Khan and Simple Minds will headline Radio 2 in the Park, BBC Radio 2's flagship music festival. The three-day event runs from September 11-13 at City Park in Stirling, Scotland.

cards.headline: Cannes screenplay winner secures international distribution deals
cards.teaser: Emmanuel Marre's film has been picked up by distributors across Europe following its festival premiere.
cards.body:
Charades has signed distribution deals for Emmanuel Marre's A Man of His Time across multiple territories following its world premiere at Cannes, where the French-Belgian drama won the best screenplay award. The Paris-based sales company secured agreements with Frenetic Films for Switzerland, Filmin for Spain, Alamode Film for Germany, and I Wonder Pictures for Italy.

The film's Cannes recognition and critical reception have generated strong international interest among buyers, positioning it for wider release across Europe and Asia.

cards.headline: Ten young European filmmakers selected for Karlovy Vary festival program
cards.teaser: The Future Frames initiative will showcase emerging directing talent at the Czech festival next month.
cards.body:
European Film Promotion has announced ten young filmmakers selected for the Future Frames program at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival next month. The initiative supports emerging European cinema talent and is organized by European Film Promotion in cooperation with the festival.

Future Frames is returning to the Czech festival, offering a platform for the next generation of European directors. The program provides opportunities for participants to showcase their work and connect with industry professionals at one of Europe's leading film festivals.

cards.headline: Icelandic producer Sigurjón Sighvatsson to receive honor at Locarno Film Festival
cards.teaser: The co-founder of Propaganda Films will be celebrated with an award recognizing independent producers.
cards.body:
Sigurjón Sighvatsson will receive the Raimondo Rezzonico Award at the Locarno Film Festival, recognizing his career as a producer embodying the independent film ethos. The Icelandic producer co-founded Propaganda Films with Steve Golin in 1986, building the company into a powerhouse producing film, music videos, and television.

Propaganda Films produced hit television shows including Twin Peaks under Sighvatsson's leadership. The award honors producers who have made significant contributions to independent cinema throughout their careers, with Sighvatsson joining previous recipients celebrated for their work outside traditional studio systems.

hero.headline: Trump nominates Todd Blanche as attorney general
hero.body:
President Trump formally nominated Todd Blanche to serve as attorney general on Monday, positioning his former personal lawyer to become the nation's top law enforcement officer. The nomination will require Senate confirmation to become permanent.

Blanche has been serving in an acting capacity since April, when Trump fired Pam Bondi from the role. Bondi faced criticism for her handling of the Epstein files, an issue that has followed the president for years. Trump previously described Blanche as "a very talented guy" while discussing the nomination on a podcast.

Blanche previously represented Trump in several high-profile legal cases. He was Trump's attorney in the hush-money case involving adult film actor Stormy Daniels, which resulted in Trump's conviction on 34 felony counts for fraudulently falsifying business records. Blanche also represented Trump in the federal classified documents case and election obstruction cases, both of which were dismissed following Trump's electoral victory.

As acting attorney general, Blanche has pursued controversial actions under the banner of combating what the administration calls "weaponization" of the Justice Department. Federal prosecutors have filed criminal charges against James Comey, the former FBI director, and escalated investigations into former CIA director John Brennan. The department also removed press releases about prosecutions related to the January 6 Capitol attack.

Republican Senate Judiciary Committee Chair Chuck Grassley called Blanche "well-qualified," stating he has "worked well with acting attorney general Blanche for more than a year and appreciate his commitment to transparency and support for law enforcement."

Democratic opposition is expected to be significant. Senator Adam Schiff of California argued that "at every turn, Todd Blanche has been unable to put aside his role as Donald Trump's criminal defense lawyer and represent the American people instead." Schiff highlighted several controversial decisions, including support for the Comey indictment based on an Instagram photo and approval of a 1.8 billion dollar fund to compensate Trump supporters who claimed they faced political persecution.

Blanche also signed a Justice Department memo granting Trump, his sons, and the Trump Organization immunity from IRS audits and tax prosecutions. Representative Rosa DeLauro, a Connecticut Democrat, criticized this action, saying that "when you are issuing memos granting the president, his children, and their companies immunity from audits or prosecution for tax offenses, your previous role becomes relevant information."

The controversial compensation fund faced bipartisan criticism. Republican Brian Fitzpatrick from Pennsylvania drafted legislation with bipartisan support to block its creation. Under mounting pressure, Blanche announced on Tuesday that the fund had been terminated.

Republicans hold the Senate majority, which could facilitate confirmation, though some lawmakers have indicated they plan to review Blanche's record closely. The Senate Judiciary Committee typically schedules hearings within weeks of a formal nomination.

cards.headline: Congress faces deadline to renew warrantless surveillance powers
cards.teaser: A deadline to reauthorize Section 702 surveillance powers collides with controversy over a White House intelligence appointment.
cards.body:
The deadline to renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act is approaching as Democrats increasingly oppose reauthorization due to the White House appointment of Bill Pulte to lead the intelligence community. The warrantless spy powers allow intelligence agencies to monitor foreign targets.

A growing number of Democrats have said they will not vote to renew Section 702 while Pulte's appointment remains in place. The collision between the reauthorization deadline and the pressure campaign over Pulte's nomination creates uncertainty about whether Congress will extend the surveillance authority before it expires.

cards.headline: U.S.-Iran war reaches 100 days with no resolution
cards.teaser: The conflict between the United States and Iran has continued for over three months despite Trump's campaign pledges to avoid prolonged foreign wars.
cards.body:
The war between the United States and Iran reached its 100-day mark over the weekend with no clear path to resolution. President Trump had campaigned on promises to keep the country out of extended foreign conflicts.

Trump responded to questions about the war's duration by denying he had ever promised not to start new wars. He also disputed characterizations of the conflict with Iran as an endless war. The fighting has now extended well beyond initial expectations, with no timeline for conclusion.

cards.headline: Trust in federal health agencies fell sharply in Trump's first year
cards.teaser: Public confidence in the CDC and other federal health institutions declined significantly during the first year of Trump's second term, according to a new poll.
cards.body:
Trust in federal health institutions dropped considerably during the first year of President Trump's second administration, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention seeing particularly sharp declines. A poll by Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and the de Beaumont Foundation's Public Health Listening Lab found the decline in trust has become deeply partisan.

The survey measured public attitudes toward federal health agencies one year into Trump's return to office. The findings show a significant shift in how Americans view institutions like the CDC, with trust levels varying sharply along political lines.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Haaland's victory sets up a general election campaign where she could make history.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She previously served as Secretary of the Interior under President Biden before launching her gubernatorial campaign.

cards.headline: Trump endorsement tested in South Carolina GOP gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette in a crowded Republican field that includes the state attorney general and sitting congressmen.
cards.body:
The South Carolina Republican gubernatorial primary offered another test of President Trump's influence following his first major statewide primary loss last week. Trump endorsed Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette over several prominent Republicans in the race.

The GOP field includes state Attorney General Alan Wilson and Representative Ralph Norman. The primary result will indicate whether Trump's endorsement power remains strong among Republican voters after recent setbacks in other states.

cards.headline: Maine Democrats express concern over primary candidate Graham Platner
cards.teaser: The oyster farmer and political newcomer faces scrutiny over controversies as Democrats select their Senate candidate.
cards.body:
Democrats heading into Maine's primary expressed anxiety about Graham Platner, an oyster farmer and political newcomer whose campaign has been marked by controversies. The unease among party members came as they prepared to select their nominee on Tuesday.

Democrats view the Maine Senate race as a potential pickup opportunity in the fall election, making the primary selection particularly significant for the party.
